With the start of a new school year, a growing number of Americans now support a complete ban on students using phones in classrooms.

The new school year is underway, and calls to prohibit iPhones in schools continue to grow louder.

That's right — although it's still July, summer seems to have already come to an end. My kids are heading back to school today and tomorrow, marking the second consecutive summer that the first day of school is no longer in August.

Apple is welcoming the new school year with its annual "Back to School" promotion. Eligible students and educators who purchase select Mac and iPad models by August 27 can receive a gift card worth up to $150. Consumers in participating states can also take advantage of limited-time sales tax holiday offers.

While back-to-school deals are exciting, phone use during class is becoming increasingly unpopular.

Top comment posted by GreenPizza

I've never seen any data supporting allowing students to use phones during school shootings to reduce risk. Actually, reducing distractions in the classroom is what truly allows us to accomplish the purpose of going to school.

A new Pew Research Center survey found that 77% of American adults support banning middle and high school students from using phones in classrooms, up from 68% in 2024 and 74% in 2025. Only 18% currently oppose such bans in schools.

Support for stricter all-day bans — prohibiting students from using phones throughout the entire school day — has risen even more significantly. For the first time, the number of Americans backing all-day bans has surpassed those opposed.

The report also noted that younger adults remain less enthusiastic about classroom bans and all-day bans, but support has risen across all age groups since 2024. The full report can be read here.

What do you think? Should schools restrict students to using iPhones only during class, implement an all-day ban, or leave the decision to students and parents? Let us know in the comments.
